catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ahriman-and-o: Ahriman and Ormuzd, more correctly Ormuzd and Ahriman, are the Persian forms, modern, of Anro-Mainyus and Ahura Mazda. They are, respectively, the Avestic or Zoroastrian religion's Evil and Good Spirits, of ancient Iranians and modern Parsees. The two names embody the faith's dualism: a good spirit opposed by an evil spirit, each contending for the world.
